reasoning_summary: Mean drag is not statistically settled to the 3 % tolerance. The stationary window has only 3 cycles. The 95 % CI on mean Cd is 0.044509, which is about 3.4 % of 1.3039 and already above 3 %. The relative drift of mean Cd is 0.040105, also above 3 %.

The stationary-window start (15.276 convective units) is flagged as the MSER cap. The record may therefore still contain transient, and the averaging window is not reliably identified. The declared averaging start was 10.0. The Cd means differ between the submitted setup (1.2961) and the window (1.3039), which shows sensitivity to window choice.

The Strouhal frequency resolution is 0.033333, about 20 % of the reported St of about 0.16. That is far coarser than the 3 % tolerance. The two estimates, 0.16058 (window) and 0.16169 (FFT), agree with each other, and the submitted setup gave 0.16129. Their agreement is on the order of 1 %, which is finer than the stated resolution, so this does not demonstrate 3 % accuracy. With only 3 cycles in 40 convective units, St is weakly constrained.

The mesh is coarse for resolving the wake and shear layers. It has a representative cell size of 0.45745 D, a wake last cell of 1.0209 D, and 30580 cells. No mesh or time-step refinement evidence is available, so discretisation error on Cd and St cannot be bounded to 3 %. The linearUpwind scheme with 1 outer corrector adds further uncertainty.

The setup is otherwise sound: the inlet is uniform, blockage is 0.0125, the force reference matches the problem specification, Courant is 0.73373, and mass imbalance is negligible. These points do not offset the unquantified statistical and discretisation uncertainty, so neither quantity can be trusted to 3 %.
